job:
In front of you, on a counter, is a box with a lid, shut. A knob -- a cube
26 mm on a side -- hangs from its front, and it carries tag 53 on
every face.

Open the lid -- past 57 degrees from shut -- then set
it back down shut, and let go of it. While it is open more than
5 degrees the lid must never come down faster than
1.0 rad/s: let fall, it is not set down. The world grades
the job when your procedure ends and again 5 s later: the lid
must be shut by then, and nothing of yours may touch the lid, its knob or its
handle. A try may take 68 s at most. If you fall during a try or
in the 5 s after it, the try fails, however the lid ends.

vocabulary.heading: the language
vocabulary.text:
THE LANGUAGE

A procedure is Python-SHAPED text, read and never executed, and it may use
only what is listed here. It is checked whole before anything moves and
refused, with the line at fault, if it uses anything else. Its source may
be at most 3,000 characters.

  def wave():                         # first in the source, the def that runs: no arguments, a lowercase name
      budget(steps=40, seconds=60)    # optional, first; steps at most 200, seconds at most 1800
      n = 0
      reach("right", 0.25, -0.30, 1.30)
      for i in range(3):              # a literal count
          move_hand("right", 0.25, -0.20, 1.30)
          move_hand("right", 0.25, -0.40, 1.30)
          n += 1
      if read("right.z") > 1.0:
          withdraw("right")

Statements: a verb call, `name = expr`, `name += expr`, `if/elif/else`,
`for name in range(N)` (N at most 100), `while` (stopped at 100 rounds),
`pass`, `return` (alone), and first in the def that runs, `budget(...)`:
the most verbs the run calls (`steps`) and the most seconds it runs
(`seconds`), 60 verbs and 600 seconds without one.
Every name you choose is lowercase letters, digits and underscores, a letter first, at most 32 characters.
Expressions: numbers, your variables,
`read("sensor")`, + - * /, comparisons, `and`/`or`/`not`. Nothing else: no
other calls but your defs' (below), no strings but a name a verb, a read or
a def is given, no imports -- but
`sin(a)`, `cos(a)` (a in radians), `atan2(y, x)` and `sqrt(v)` may be used
in an expression. A procedure runs until it ends, a verb fails, you fall, its
budget runs out or it has run 100,000 statements; a verb fails when the
world says it did not do what it said -- and then the procedure stops there. A verb's numbers come back only
through `read`, and your variables are your readout.
A source may hold several defs, all within its 3,000 characters. The
first is the procedure, and runs, so it goes above the defs it calls; each
def after it is one it may call by its name -- a statement of its own --
and they may call each other, with arguments as a verb takes them, in
order or by keyword, each a number or a name in quotes:

  def greet():
      sway("left", 0.30, 0.25)
      sway("right", 0.30, -0.25, 1.20)

  def sway(hand, x, y, z=1.30):       # z is 1.30 where a call leaves it out
      reach(hand, x, y, z)
      high = read(hand + ".z") + 0.05
      move_hand(hand, x, y + 0.10, high)
      withdraw(hand)

An argument a def uses where a verb or `read` takes a name holds a name,
and names join with + (`hand + ".z"`); any other holds a number. A call
does what its def does, and stops the procedure where its def stops short:
a verb in it failed, or its arithmetic did. A def's variables are its own,
and its last ones ride your readout after yours (`sway.high`). The first
def takes no argument without a default; a def may not call itself,
through another or not, and calls go at most 4 deep. The run has the
first def's budget, and every call spends from it.
A verb may also stand alone as the test of an `if` or an `elif` -- `if
move_hand("left", 0.3, 0.2, 0.9):` or `if not reach(...):` -- and then it
runs as the test: true when it did what it said, false when it did not,
and its failing does not stop the procedure. So may a call: true when its def
ran to its end or a `return`, false where it stopped short. But if
you fall, the procedure stops there, in a test or not.
A hand's move may stop on a sensor: `reach`, `move_hand` and `pull` each
take one stop condition, by keyword after their other arguments --
`until="<sensor>"` and `above=N` or `below=N`, N a number your procedure
may compute. The move then stops where the hand is the first time that
sensor reads more than N (`above`) or less than N (`below`), and holds
there -- at once, if it already does -- and the verb is ok; after it,
`reach.stopped`, `move_hand.stopped` or `pull.stopped` reads 1, and 0
after a move that ended otherwise. A move reads its sensor as often as
your body reads it, and no oftener: a hand's place, force and grip, and
the time, 100 times a second; what `watch` reads, 15 times a second. A hand's force it reads from
0.1 s into the move: a move's start reads the move itself, and a hand
moving through the air reads up to 12 N with nothing touched. What a
verb last reported (`spot.*`, `pull.*` and the like) no move changes, so no
move stops on it. A hand carried to your left that stops where it pushes on
something with 15 N:
    move_hand("right", 0.30, -0.05, 1.20, until="right.fy", above=15)

vocabulary.heading: your body
vocabulary.text:
YOUR BODY

Every place is in your STANCE frame, in metres: from the floor between your
feet, x straight ahead, y to your left, z up. The frame moves with your
feet, and taking a posture to reach can move them a little: a place you
read before a reach may lie elsewhere in the frame after it. Your shoulders are 1.15 m up,
4 cm behind your feet's middle and 0.18 m either side of it; an arm held
straight puts its grip 0.58 m from its shoulder, and it reaches less far
with its hand turned some ways. Your trunk turns on a waist over your hips,
up to 60 degrees either way, your shoulders and your head with it. Your hands are "left" and "right": each ends in a two-jaw gripper
whose jaws close across the point between them (its grip), its fingers 8 cm
long. Both grippers start shut. A hand that is OUT is one you have reached
with, until you withdraw it. Before a `step` or any other walk, a hand that
is out comes home, its gripper opened as `withdraw` opens it: a walk carries
nothing.

VERBS (a statement each; arguments in this order, or by keyword)
  wait(seconds)  -- stand still
  move(axis, target)  -- walk one axis to a setpoint, ramped, inside its envelope
  spot(tag)  -- stand still and look for this tag in your colour camera -- as you stand, then bowing lower until you see it -- and stand up again; ok when you see it. That camera looks down, lower than your navigation camera: its picture runs from 19 to 61 degrees below level, out to 34 degrees either side of where your head faces at its top and more than 50 at its bottom, and bowing only takes it lower. With your trunk square to your feet, a thing at x in your stance frame is in the picture only if it stands lower than (1.27 - 0.34 x) m over the floor, and a tag reads only with the whole of it inside the picture: the lower a tag is, the further off it reads, a small one level with your shoulders only within about 0.3 m ahead of you, a larger one nearer still, and nothing as high as your camera ever. Inside the picture, a small block's tag reads from up to about 1.5 m away. Where its face is, which way the face looks and which way its edges run ride `spot.*`. A small block carries its tag on every face: the one read is the one you see most square-on, `spot.nx`..`nz` say which, so from elsewhere the same tag can read another face, its middle up to the block's width from this one's. A tag is named by its number, not in quotes: `spot(12)` looks for tag 12
  watch(tag)  -- keep your colour camera reading this tag while your procedure goes on -- your hands moving, your feet stepping, waiting -- 15 times a second, each reading yours 0.1 s after its picture was taken; it neither bows nor turns to look, and it ends with your procedure or your next `watch`. It reads through `spot`'s camera, the top of whose picture is 19 degrees below level as you stand and lower as you bow: what is above that, it cannot see. It waits for its first reading; ok when that shows the tag (as an `if`'s test that is not, it watches on). What it reads rides `watch.*`: of a small block, as for `spot`, the face that picture shows most square-on, so which face can change as you move. A tag is named by its number, not in quotes: `watch(12)` keeps reading tag 12
  reach(hand, x, y, z, fx=0, fy=0, fz=0, jx=0, jy=0, jz=0, stiffness=1[, until, above, below])  -- send a hand's grip -- the point between its jaws -- to (x, y, z), its fingers pointing along (fx, fy, fz) and its jaws closing along (jx, jy, jz) -- either way, a two-jaw grip -- or at whatever turn your arm finds where those are all left 0. It goes out to a point short of it, then in along the fingers; you take whatever posture reaches. stiffness 1 is your arm's full stiffness, less is softer. ok once it holds there -- or as near as it came: what it touches on its way in can hold it a few cm short, and your hand's place (`left.x` and the rest) says where it is. Given `until` (a sensor) and `above` or `below` (a number), it stops sooner -- where the hand is, as soon as that sensor reads past that number -- and is ok then too
  via(hand, x, y, z, fx=0, fy=0, fz=0, jx=0, jy=0, jz=0)  -- add the point (x, y, z) to your hand's path, the grip turned there to (fx, fy, fz) and (jx, jy, jz) where given as for `reach`; nothing moves until your next `move_hand`, which goes through the path's points on its way
  move_hand(hand, x, y, z, speed=0.06, stiffness=1, fx=0, fy=0, fz=0, jx=0, jy=0, jz=0[, until, above, below])  -- carry a hand that is out (reached) to (x, y, z) at `speed` m/s along a straight line -- or through the points `via` added first, in turn, as one motion from one posture that follows them all, turning as each asks (a point with no turn keeps the one before); the path is then empty -- its turn kept, or turned to (fx, fy, fz) and (jx, jy, jz) given as for `reach`; ok when it arrives. Given `until` (a sensor) and `above` or `below` (a number), it stops sooner -- where the hand is, as soon as that sensor reads past that number -- and is ok then too
  pull(hand, dx, dy, dz, force, distance, speed=0.06, give=1[, until, above, below])  -- pull a hand that is out -- or push it -- along the way (dx, dy, dz), of any length, with at most `force` N, at most `speed` m/s: across that way your hand goes where what it holds pushes it, and its turn gives to what it holds, but about the line its jaws close along (what it holds turns about that line between the jaws) -- or, `give` 0, it holds its line and its turn. It stops once it has gone `distance` m along the way, it is held fast (pushing with its whole force and not moving), its grip lets go, or it can reach no further; then it holds there. Standing, your body holds a pull of 20 N at a hand, and pushing away from you around two thirds of that. How far it went, the hardest it pushed, whether it ended held fast and the way it was going at its end ride `pull.*`, unless it reads false; ok unless an argument was refused, your hand was not out, (dx, dy, dz) are all 0 or you fell: whatever else stopped it, held fast against something too, it is still ok, and `pull.moved` says how far it went. Given `until` (a sensor) and `above` or `below` (a number), it stops sooner -- where the hand is, as soon as that sensor reads past that number -- and is ok then too
  close_hand(hand, force=120)  -- shut a hand's gripper where it is, squeezing with at most `force` N a jaw -- firm holds fast; light lets what it holds turn between the jaws; ok when it says it holds something
  open_hand(hand)  -- open a hand's gripper
  withdraw(hand)  -- open a hand's gripper, letting go of whatever it holds, then bring the hand back out along the way it went in, and its arm home -- straight there, or out to your side first and down at your side where that keeps the arm higher in front of you than straight would; ok once your arm is home
  step(ahead, left=0, turn=0)  -- turn `turn` rad on the spot (left, +), then walk `ahead` m and `left` m in the frame you then stand in (negative: back, right), and stand still -- your hands home first; a step carries nothing. Your feet walk in strides, each carrying your stance about 5 cm: a walk asked under 6 cm may take none, and a walk may stop a few cm off what you asked. A walk asked at least 1 cm that your own legs count as under it reads false and says your step was too short to walk. A walk keeps off another robot as your walks over the map do. It stops before it would take your middle within 0.65 m of that robot's middle (1.2 m of one that has fallen) -- standing within that already, a step whose walk would take you nearer neither turns nor walks -- and once that robot's body is within 0.4 m of your middle in the way you step and 0.27 m either side of it. Either reads false and says so. A turn lands within a degree or two of what you asked -- one that does not get there reads false and says so -- and shuffles your feet a few cm that `step.*` does not count. `step.dy` counts a sidestep 1-3 cm short of how far your feet went, and one going left after a step ahead up to 10 cm or more short. Your stance frame goes with your feet: where they went in the frame you stood in before rides `step.*` (`step.dx` ahead, `step.dy` left, m, and `step.turn`, rad), so a place (x, y) you read before is now (c (x - dx) + s (y - dy), c (y - dy) - s (x - dx)), c and s the cosine and sine of its turn; ok when it stepped
  measure(x, y)  -- look with your depth camera at what stands within 0.45 m of (x, y): the height of its flat top and where that top ends -- nearest and farthest ahead, leftmost and rightmost -- ride `object.*`; ok when a flat top is seen, 0.06 m or more over the floor. An end reads only where your camera saw past it: where the top runs on past those 0.45 m, off your camera's picture or out of its range (0.17 to 3 m), its end that way has no reading, and reading it says why. Where something taller stands just past an end, that end reads where the free top stops, and `object.near_taller` (`far`, `left`, `right`) reads 1

SENSORS for `read("<sensor>")` -- one number each
  time -- sim seconds
  left.x -- where your left hand's grip is, m, your stance frame (x)
  left.y -- where your left hand's grip is, m, your stance frame (y)
  left.z -- where your left hand's grip is, m, your stance frame (z)
  left.fx -- the force your left hand pushes with, N, your stance frame (x), off your motor currents less your own weight, your joints' friction and your body's own motion -- your whole body's while that hand is out and you stand, else its arm's alone; it reads truest held still, and moving through the air up to 12 N with nothing touched
  left.fy -- the force your left hand pushes with, N, your stance frame (y), off your motor currents less your own weight, your joints' friction and your body's own motion -- your whole body's while that hand is out and you stand, else its arm's alone; it reads truest held still, and moving through the air up to 12 N with nothing touched
  left.fz -- the force your left hand pushes with, N, your stance frame (z), off your motor currents less your own weight, your joints' friction and your body's own motion -- your whole body's while that hand is out and you stand, else its arm's alone; it reads truest held still, and moving through the air up to 12 N with nothing touched
  left.held -- 1 while your left gripper says it holds something: its jaws stopped short of closed, squeezing
  left.gap -- how far apart your left gripper's jaws are, m: what it holds, how wide
  right.x -- where your right hand's grip is, m, your stance frame (x)
  right.y -- where your right hand's grip is, m, your stance frame (y)
  right.z -- where your right hand's grip is, m, your stance frame (z)
  right.fx -- the force your right hand pushes with, N, your stance frame (x), off your motor currents less your own weight, your joints' friction and your body's own motion -- your whole body's while that hand is out and you stand, else its arm's alone; it reads truest held still, and moving through the air up to 12 N with nothing touched
  right.fy -- the force your right hand pushes with, N, your stance frame (y), off your motor currents less your own weight, your joints' friction and your body's own motion -- your whole body's while that hand is out and you stand, else its arm's alone; it reads truest held still, and moving through the air up to 12 N with nothing touched
  right.fz -- the force your right hand pushes with, N, your stance frame (z), off your motor currents less your own weight, your joints' friction and your body's own motion -- your whole body's while that hand is out and you stand, else its arm's alone; it reads truest held still, and moving through the air up to 12 N with nothing touched
  right.held -- 1 while your right gripper says it holds something: its jaws stopped short of closed, squeezing
  right.gap -- how far apart your right gripper's jaws are, m: what it holds, how wide
  spot.x -- where the tag the last `spot` saw is, m, your stance frame (x): the middle of the face it read
  spot.y -- where the tag the last `spot` saw is, m, your stance frame (y): the middle of the face it read
  spot.z -- where the tag the last `spot` saw is, m, your stance frame (z): the middle of the face it read
  spot.nx -- which way that face looks (x): a unit vector from it into the thing it is printed on
  spot.ny -- which way that face looks (y): a unit vector from it into the thing it is printed on
  spot.nz -- which way that face looks (z): a unit vector from it into the thing it is printed on
  spot.ex -- which way that face's edges run (x): a unit vector along one of them, the other at right angles to it and to the face's look
  spot.ey -- which way that face's edges run (y): a unit vector along one of them, the other at right angles to it and to the face's look
  spot.ez -- which way that face's edges run (z): a unit vector along one of them, the other at right angles to it and to the face's look
  spot.range -- how far that tag was from the camera, m
  watch.x -- where the tag you watch was in the newest picture that showed it, m, your stance frame (x): the middle of the face it read
  watch.y -- where the tag you watch was in the newest picture that showed it, m, your stance frame (y): the middle of the face it read
  watch.z -- where the tag you watch was in the newest picture that showed it, m, your stance frame (z): the middle of the face it read
  watch.nx -- which way that face looked (x): a unit vector from it into the thing it is printed on
  watch.ny -- which way that face looked (y): a unit vector from it into the thing it is printed on
  watch.nz -- which way that face looked (z): a unit vector from it into the thing it is printed on
  watch.ex -- which way that face's edges ran (x): a unit vector along one of them
  watch.ey -- which way that face's edges ran (y): a unit vector along one of them
  watch.ez -- which way that face's edges ran (z): a unit vector along one of them
  watch.range -- how far that tag was from the camera then, m
  watch.seen -- 1 while your newest picture shows the tag you watch, 0 while it does not: out of view, or hidden -- by your own hand too
  watch.age -- how long ago the newest picture that showed it was taken, s: how old `watch.x` and the rest are
  pull.moved -- how far the last `pull` took the hand from where it began, m
  pull.force -- the hardest the last `pull` pushed along its way, N, as your hand felt it
  pull.held -- 1 if the last `pull` ended held fast, as your hand felt it, 0 if something else stopped it
  pull.dx -- the way your hand was going at the end of the last `pull` (x), your stance frame: a unit vector, where what it held let it go
  pull.dy -- the way your hand was going at the end of the last `pull` (y), your stance frame: a unit vector, where what it held let it go
  pull.dz -- the way your hand was going at the end of the last `pull` (z), your stance frame: a unit vector, where what it held let it go
  step.dx -- how far ahead your feet went in the last `step`, m, in the stance frame you stood in before it
  step.dy -- how far to your left your feet went in the last `step`, m, in that frame
  step.turn -- how far you turned in the last `step`, rad (left, +)
  object.top -- the height of the flat top `measure` last saw, m
  object.near -- how far ahead that top begins, m
  object.far -- how far ahead that top ends, m
  object.left -- how far to your left that top reaches, m
  object.right -- how far to your left its right edge is (negative: to your right), m
  object.near_taller -- 1 if something taller stands just past that top's near end, where its free surface stops (the top may go on behind it); 0 if your camera saw the top stop there
  object.far_taller -- 1 if something taller stands just past that top's far end, where its free surface stops (the top may go on behind it); 0 if your camera saw the top stop there
  object.left_taller -- 1 if something taller stands just past that top's left end, where its free surface stops (the top may go on behind it); 0 if your camera saw the top stop there
  object.right_taller -- 1 if something taller stands just past that top's right end, where its free surface stops (the top may go on behind it); 0 if your camera saw the top stop there
  reach.stopped -- 1 if your last `reach` stopped on its `until`, 0 if it ended otherwise
  move_hand.stopped -- 1 if your last `move_hand` stopped on its `until`, 0 if it ended otherwise
  pull.stopped -- 1 if your last `pull` stopped on its `until`, 0 if it ended otherwise

AXES for `move("<axis>", target)` -- one arm joint's angle, rad, walked to
it at 1 rad/s
  left_shoulder_pitch: -3.01942..1.71042 rad -- your left arm's shoulder pitch joint
  left_shoulder_roll: 0..3.03687 rad -- your left arm's shoulder roll joint
  left_shoulder_yaw: -2.05949..2.05949 rad -- your left arm's shoulder yaw joint
  left_elbow: 0..2.10312 rad -- your left arm's elbow joint
  left_wrist_pitch: -1.6..1.6 rad -- your left arm's wrist pitch joint
  left_wrist_roll: -2.05949..2.05949 rad -- your left arm's wrist roll joint
  right_shoulder_pitch: -3.01942..1.71042 rad -- your right arm's shoulder pitch joint
  right_shoulder_roll: -3.03687..-0 rad -- your right arm's shoulder roll joint
  right_shoulder_yaw: -2.05949..2.05949 rad -- your right arm's shoulder yaw joint
  right_elbow: 0..2.10312 rad -- your right arm's elbow joint
  right_wrist_pitch: -1.6..1.6 rad -- your right arm's wrist pitch joint
  right_wrist_roll: -2.05949..2.05949 rad -- your right arm's wrist roll joint

Your feet walk in strides, each carrying your stance about 5 cm: a walk asked under 6 cm may take none, and a walk may stop a few cm off what you asked. A walk asked at least 1 cm that your own legs count as under it reads false and says your step was too short to walk. A walk keeps off another robot as your walks over the map do. It stops before it would take your middle within 0.65 m of that robot's middle (1.2 m of one that has fallen) -- standing within that already, a step whose walk would take you nearer neither turns nor walks -- and once that robot's body is within 0.4 m of your middle in the way you step and 0.27 m either side of it. Either reads false and says so. A turn lands within a degree or two of what you asked -- one that does not get there reads false and says so -- and shuffles your feet a few cm that `step.*` does not count. `step.dy` counts a sidestep 1-3 cm short of how far your feet went, and one going left after a step ahead up to 10 cm or more short. Your stance frame goes with your feet: where they went in the frame you stood in before rides `step.*` (`step.dx` ahead, `step.dy` left, m, and `step.turn`, rad), so a place (x, y) you read before is now (c (x - dx) + s (y - dy), c (y - dy) - s (x - dx)), c and s the cosine and sine of its turn; ok when it stepped

look with your depth camera at what stands within 0.45 m of (x, y): the height of its flat top and where that top ends -- nearest and farthest ahead, leftmost and rightmost -- ride `object.*`; ok when a flat top is seen, 0.06 m or more over the floor. An end reads only where your camera saw past it: where the top runs on past those 0.45 m, off your camera's picture or out of its range (0.17 to 3 m), its end that way has no reading, and reading it says why. Where something taller stands just past an end, that end reads where the free top stops, and `object.near_taller` (`far`, `left`, `right`) reads 1
